facts.text: A standard is a written agreement produced by a committee of experts that specifies how something should be made, tested or described so that terminology and expectations are shared.
facts.quote: A standard is a written agreement, produced by a committee of experts, that says how something should be made, tested or described so that everyone means the same thing.

facts.text: A technical standard is a published document identified by a number, title and edition year; ISO 16001:2017 is an example.
facts.quote: It is a published document with a number, a title and an edition year, for example "ISO 16001:2017".

facts.text: Standards are written by volunteers from manufacturers, users, test laboratories, regulators and universities in technical committees run by standards bodies such as the International Organization for Standardization (ISO).
facts.quote: Standards are written by volunteers from manufacturers, users, test laboratories, regulators and universities, meeting in a technical committee run by a standards body such as the International Organization for Standardization (ISO).

facts.text: A draft standard undergoes rounds of comment and voting by member countries before publication; published standards are reviewed every few years and confirmed, revised or withdrawn.
facts.quote: The draft passes through rounds of comment and voting by member countries before publication, and is then reviewed every few years and confirmed, revised or withdrawn.

facts.text: Standard-development stages proceed from proposal and working draft to committee draft (CD), Draft International Standard (DIS) ballot, final draft (FDIS) ballot, proof (PRF) under publication, published standard and systematic review.
facts.quote:
A["Proposal and working draft"] --> B["Committee draft (CD)"]
    B --> C["Draft International Standard (DIS) ballot"]
    C --> D["Final draft (FDIS) ballot"]
    D --> E["Proof (PRF), under publication"]

facts.text: Standards have levels: ISO 12100 is a basic safety standard for all machines, ISO 13849 is a generic control-system standard for many machines, and ISO 21815-3 is a machine-specific type-C standard for collision avoidance on earth-moving machines.
facts.quote: basic safety standards for all machines (ISO 12100), generic standards for one aspect of many machines (ISO 13849 for control systems), and machine-specific "type-C" standards such as ISO 21815-3 for collision avoidance on earth-moving machines [Chapter 3].

facts.text: A standard is voluntary but becomes binding when a law points to it, a contract or purchase specification requires it, a regulator or insurer accepts it as proof of good practice, or a manufacturer chooses it to demonstrate application of the state of the art.
facts.quote: a contract or purchase specification requires it; a regulator or insurer accepts it as proof of good practice; or the manufacturer chooses it to show it has applied the state of the art.

facts.text: A law can point to a standard by citing it, harmonizing it in the European Union, or designating it in Great Britain.
facts.quote: a law points to it (by citing it, "harmonizing" it in the European Union or "designating" it in Great Britain)

facts.text: ISO, European EN and Australian AS documents are standards, whereas OSHA and MSHA rules, European Union regulations and South African mine regulations are law; compliance with standards does not prove compliance with law, or vice versa.
facts.quote: ISO, European EN and Australian AS documents are standards, while the rules of the United States workplace and mine safety agencies (OSHA and MSHA), European Union regulations and South African mine regulations are law

facts.text: ISO 16001's 300 millisecond detection limit binds an Australian quarry only if a contract or regulator requires compliance with AS ISO 16001.
facts.quote: ISO 16001's 300 millisecond detection limit binds an Australian quarry only if a contract or regulator says "comply with AS ISO 16001".

facts.text: The project's core off-road documents—ISO 21815, ISO 16001, ISO 3450 and ISO 19014—are standards rather than laws.
facts.quote: Every core off-road document for this project (ISO 21815, ISO 16001, ISO 3450, ISO 19014) is a standard, not a law

facts.text: Most of the project's core off-road standards—ISO 21815, ISO 16001, ISO 3450 and ISO 19014—are being reissued in late 2026, shortly before the design freeze.
facts.quote: Every core off-road document for this project (ISO 21815, ISO 16001, ISO 3450, ISO 19014) is a standard, not a law, and most are being reissued in late 2026, shortly before the design is frozen [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The off-road collision-mitigation project plan must track which standard binds in each market and baseline the editions actually published at the design freeze.
facts.quote: The plan must track which standard binds in which market, baseline the editions actually published at the freeze

facts.text: The booklet found no off-road standard that permits simulation to replace a prescribed physical test.
facts.quote: no off-road standard found by the booklet lets simulation replace a prescribed physical test [Chapter 3].
